reference.source: Scriver's OMMBID (Online Metabolic and Molecular Bases of Inherited Disease)
clinicalPearls: Comprises two biochemically distinct enantiomeric disorders identified by chiral separation of urinary 2-hydroxyglutarate into D and L forms

L-2-hydroxyglutaric aciduria (L2HGDH defect) causes a fairly characteristic leukoencephalopathy with subcortical white-matter and dentate/basal ganglia involvement, cerebellar signs, and progressive cognitive decline

D-2-hydroxyglutaric aciduria has two genetic subtypes: type I from D2HGDH deficiency and type II from gain-of-function IDH2 mutation, the latter often more severe with cardiomyopathy and epileptic encephalopathy
D-2-hydroxyglutarate is an oncometabolite: the IDH-related pathway links it to gliomas and other tumours, and L-2-hydroxyglutaric aciduria carries an increased lifetime risk of brain tumours
The diagnostic signature is elevated urinary 2-hydroxyglutarate, with chiral chromatography needed to determine whether the D or L enantiomer predominates
Neuroimaging patterns help differentiate the forms, with L2HGA showing a distinctive symmetric subcortical leukoencephalopathy
Both are autosomal recessive except IDH2-related D-2-HGA type II; management is largely supportive with surveillance for tumour and cardiac complications
reference.pathophysiology: 2-hydroxyglutarate exists as D and L enantiomers, normally kept low by the FAD-dependent dehydrogenases D-2-hydroxyglutarate dehydrogenase and L-2-hydroxyglutarate dehydrogenase, which return them to 2-oxoglutarate. Deficiency of either enzyme allows the corresponding enantiomer to accumulate. Accumulated 2-hydroxyglutarate acts as a competitive inhibitor of 2-oxoglutarate-dependent dioxygenases, disturbing DNA and histone demethylation and cellular metabolism; the D enantiomer in particular is a recognised oncometabolite connected to the IDH mutation pathway seen in gliomas. In D-2-HGA type II, mutant IDH2 gains the capacity to produce D-2-hydroxyglutarate directly. These mechanisms explain the progressive neurological injury, the leukoencephalopathy of the L form, and the increased tumour risk.
additionalDifferentials: Combined D,L-2-hydroxyglutaric aciduria (SLC25A1-related, more severe neonatal encephalopathy)
Glutaric aciduria type I with basal ganglia involvement
Other organic acidurias causing epileptic encephalopathy

Canavan disease and other white-matter disorders
additionalInvestigations: Urine organic acids with chiral separation to quantify D- and L-2-hydroxyglutarate
Brain MRI to characterise the leukoencephalopathy and deep grey-matter pattern
Molecular analysis of L2HGDH, D2HGDH, and IDH2
Cardiac evaluation (echocardiography) particularly in D-2-HGA type II
Tumour surveillance given the malignancy association, especially in the L form
redFlags: New or progressive neurological deficit that may signal an intracranial tumour
Cardiomyopathy and epileptic encephalopathy suggesting IDH2-related D-2-HGA type II
Neonatal severe encephalopathy suggesting the combined D,L form
reference.prognosis: Outcome varies by form: L-2-hydroxyglutaric aciduria typically causes slowly progressive neurological decline with a raised tumour risk, whereas D-2-HGA ranges from relatively mild (type I) to severe early encephalopathy with cardiomyopathy (type II). Care is supportive with surveillance for complications.
pitfalls: Reporting total 2-hydroxyglutarate without chiral separation, missing the crucial D-versus-L distinction
Overlooking the increased brain-tumour risk and omitting surveillance
Failing to evaluate the heart in D-2-HGA type II
Confusing it with the more severe combined D,L-2-hydroxyglutaric aciduria
references: Nyhan, Atlas of Inherited Metabolic Diseases
management: Consider a trial of riboflavin (flavin adenine dinucleotide precursor) supplementation in L-2-hydroxyglutaric aciduria given the FAD-dependent dehydrogenase defect, as an adjunct of uncertain benefit
Antiseizure medication tailored to seizure type for the associated epilepsy or epileptic encephalopathy
Supportive neurorehabilitation with physiotherapy, occupational and speech-and-language therapy for the progressive motor, cerebellar and cognitive decline
Cardiac surveillance by echocardiography with heart-failure treatment for the cardiomyopathy of D-2-hydroxyglutaric aciduria type II
Regular neuroimaging and clinical surveillance for brain tumours given the raised malignancy risk, particularly in the L form
Coordinate care through metabolic medicine, neurology, cardiology and rehabilitation services
Offer genetic counselling and testing of L2HGDH, D2HGDH or IDH2 for the family, distinguishing the germline IDH2 change of type II
